items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:44:1
items.html:
When you count the name from AB etc., and when we count the name from the discernment of SAG alone etc.: And we must know that the relation of Taamim, Nekudot, Tagin and letters to the four-letter name differs from the relation of the ten Sefirot or the five Partzufim to the four-letter name. For according to the ten Sefirot, the tip of the Yod is regarded as Keter, and the Yod as Hochma, and the Hey as Bina, and the Vav as ZA, and the last Hey as Malchut. However, according to Taamim, Nekudot, Tagin and letters, the Yod is regarded as Taamim and Keter, and the first Hey as Nekudot and Hochma, and the Vav as Tagin and Bina, and the lower Hey as letters and ZON. And the reason for this is that the four degrees of Taamim, Nekudot, Tagin and letters are merely four values that come in the order of the departure of the lights of the Partzufim before the correction, as the ARI wrote of them above (item 9): that the first expansion from the Malchut of the Rosh [head] to the Guf [body] is called Taamim, since it is direct light and mercy, and that vessel is called Keter, because the lights first come to the Guf always in the vessel of Keter; and it is called the Yod of HaVaYaH, because it is the beginning of the clothing of the Guf and the vessels, and it is therefore attributed to the Yod, which is the beginning of HaVaYaH. And when the screen in the vessel of Keter is refined, and the level goes on diminishing through the four phases until it disappears entirely into the Emanator, all those four levels are called Nekudot, since they are emanated at the time when the lights depart to the Emanator, and are therefore regarded as reflected light and judgment; and they are called Hochma because the upper Sefira among them is Hochma, and the three levels Bina, ZA and Malchut are included in the upper one. And they are called the first Hey of HaVaYaH for the reason that they are judgment, and judgment is always regarded as the Nukva, who is the Hey of HaVaYaH. And the records that remain after the departure of the light of the Taamim are called Tagin [crowns], since they hover over the vessels at the time when their lights depart, in the likeness of Tagin over letters; and they are called Bina because they come from direct light and mercy, and they are GAR [first three]. Yet because they are in a state of departure, they are regarded as Bina, who is the Nukva of GAR. And the records from the light of the Nekudot after their departure are called letters, that is, vessels, since they come from reflected light and judgment, and also because they are from a state of departure; therefore they are regarded as vessels. And they are likewise called ZON, because the light of ZON, which is VAK [six ends], is the light of the vessels.
Thus you find that both the records of Taamim, which are called Tagin and Bina, and the records of Nekudot, which are called letters, are a state of departure and posterior. However, the record of Taamim, being GAR, is called Bina, and it is also the Vav of HaVaYaH, that is, a Vav in the Rosh; whereas the record of Nekudot, being VAK, is called ZON and letters, and they are the last Hey of HaVaYaH.
Now, the ARI’s intention here is to show the state and the degree at which the Partzuf of Nekudim stands among the Partzufim of AK, as well as the order of its cascading from them and its connection with them. He therefore first arranged for us the five Partzufim according to the four-letter name, saying that AB, which is the Partzuf of Hochma of AK, is the Yod of HaVaYaH, and that SAG, which is the Partzuf of Bina of AK, is the Hey of HaVaYaH. And after we have learned that SAG is the Hey of HaVaYaH, he details for us SAG itself as well, from the perspective of the Taamim, Nekudot, Tagin and letters within it, whose order differs from the order of the five Partzufim, as above, though they bear a close relation to one another, as we explained above.

items.html:
And when we further divide the Taamim. This division came about after the ascent of the lights from NHY of AK as MAN [female waters] to the Taamim of SAG, and to the
Nikvey Einayim of the Rosh of the Taamim. As above, page 404, item 14, that this caused there the division of the ten Sefirot of the Rosh of SAG into two discernments over the Nikvey Einayim, because of the screen and the place of the coupling that had risen there. Therefore, from the Nikvey Einayim upward it became a Rosh, and from the Nikvey Einayim downward it became a Guf, and the Ozen, Hotem and Peh that are there turned out to have gone out from the degree of Rosh to the degree of Guf. See there.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:44:3
items.html:
The letter Yod in the Ozen, and the first Hey in the Hotem, and the letter Vav in the Peh, and the last Hey in the Einayim. As was explained in the adjacent item, all this was caused by the ascent of the lights of NHY of AK to the Nikvey Einayim. For at that time the Nekudot of SAG, which are the four levels — Hochma, Bina, ZA and Malchut — which emerged in SAG after the refinement of the screen of the Keter of the Guf of SAG that is called Taamim, were expanding below the Tabur of the inner AK and were illuminating the inner ZON that are there. Thus two kinds of lights, the Nekudot of SAG and the inner ZON, are mingled with one another, SAG being phase two and the first Hey of HaVaYaH, and the inner ZON being phase four and the bottom Hey of HaVaYaH (as above, page 397, the passage beginning “AVI,” and page 395, the passage beginning “They rose”). And there the reason for the ascent of these two Heys as MAN to the Nikvey Einayim was explained, as well as the matter of their division into two degrees; study it there well, throughout the whole passage. And this is what he says, that the last Hey rose to the Nikvey Einayim, that is, through her joining with the first Hey, and that AHP therefore went outside the Rosh, this AHP being YHV [Yod-Hey-Vav]. That is, they are regarded as a lower Rosh that has a complete ten Sefirot, except for the last Hey, which is missing from them because she remained in the Nikvey Einayim.
And this is what he says: YHV in AHP, and the last Hey in the Einayim. For now the Rosh of the Taamim has been divided into two Roshim: the last Hey remained in the first Rosh, which is Galgalta ve Einayim, and in the second Rosh there is no more than YHV, where YH are KHB and the Vav is HGT NHY, as is known; and Malchut, which is the secret of the bottom Hey, is missing in the second Rosh.
And in order to understand these two Roshim, we must learn them from the Partzuf of Nekudim that emerged through this coupling in the Nikvey Einayim. For the place in which this coupling occurred, which is the Rosh of SAG, was itself not changed at all by the division that was made over the Nikvey Einayim, as above (page 392, the passage beginning “Now, although”; study it there well). Rather, only that level which emerged from this coupling in the Nikvey Einayim received all those changes that branch out from the ascent of the bottom Hey to the Nikvey Einayim; and that level, which emerged from there, is called the world of Nekudim.
And know that three Roshim are to be discerned there, in that world of Nekudim. And all three Roshim are but the ten Sefirot of a single Rosh, in terms of what they were before the ascent of MAN to the Nikvey Einayim. And you must remember the order of the ascent of the lights for the coupling of the two Partzufim AB and SAG that preceded this. For after the departure of the lights from the upper Partzuf, the two upper records rise for a coupling in the Rosh of the upper one, from which the lower one is born. They are regarded as male and female, and they first make two couplings in the Rosh of the upper one and are included in one another; and from there they descend and expand to their place in the Guf of the upper one that pertains to them, and there they once again expand of themselves into a Rosh and a Guf, as above (Part 3, Chapter 4, item 50, and page 395, the passage beginning “They rose”; study it there well).
It thus follows that after the records of the Nekudot of SAG rose with the bottom Hey to the Nikvey Einayim of the Rosh of SAG and were included there in the two couplings, they returned to their place at the Tabur of AK and expanded there into a Rosh and a Guf, in the image of the couplings they had made in the Rosh, that is, in the place of the Nikvey Einayim. And it has already been explained that the screen of the Nikvey Einayim stands at the Tabur (as above, page 401, the passage beginning “Parsa”), that is, in the place of the Parsa that was established there. It therefore turns out that the Rosh of this Partzuf emerged from the Tabur upward as far as the Chazeh [chest] of SAG, and it contains only the two Sefirot Galgalta ve Einayim, where the bottom Hey is in these Nikvey Einayim. And this is the first Rosh in the Partzuf of Nekudim, and it is reckoned on the order of the Radla [the unknown head] of Atzilut, for it does not join at all with the Partzuf of Nekudim, as above (page 409, the passage beginning “The GAR in them”); rather, it is an upper root for the Partzuf of the Nikvey Einayim.
Now the three Sefirot of the Rosh — Ozen, Hotem and Peh — which went out from the degree of the first Rosh because they are found below its screen, include two Roshim. For they are regarded as the three Sefirot AHP with respect to what is missing from the first Rosh, which is called YESHSUT; but in and of themselves they have a complete ten Sefirot, GE and AHP. And these are what are called the GAR of Nekudim, standing from the Tabur of AK downward. And they are the very substance of Nekudim, in which those two couplings of Katnut [smallness] and Gadlut [greatness] operate: for in Katnut the bottom Hey is in the Einayim of that Rosh, and the three Sefirot AHP are regarded as a lower Rosh and as HGT with respect to the upper one, which is the second Rosh, since it is below its Nikvey Einayim; and in Gadlut the bottom Hey descends to the Peh, that is, to the Malchut that includes all three Roshim, and then GE, which is the second Rosh, joins with AHP, which is the third Rosh, and they become one Rosh. Thus, from the ten Sefirot of a single Rosh, three Roshim came to be. The first Rosh, which is GE, is called YESHSUT, and it is still reckoned as Taamim and not as Nekudim. The second Rosh is the GE of the GAR of Nekudim, which is the AHP that was lacking from Israel Saba and Tevuna, and in and of themselves they contain ten Sefirot. And the third Rosh is the AHP that was lacking from the second Rosh and in and of itself became a third Rosh. And the second Rosh is the Keter of Nekudim, and the third Rosh is Hochma and Bina of Nekudim. And the bottom Hey is in the Einayim of the second Rosh, and YHV are in the third Rosh; and in the coupling of Gadlut that joins them together, when the bottom Hey descends to the Peh of the third Rosh and the two lower Roshim become one Rosh, the name HaVaYaH is found in them in its proper order, YH VH, for the bottom Hey has returned to her place.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:44:4
items.html: The eye has the discernment of the last Hey and of the first Hey. For this whole Partzuf of Nekudim, which is called the light of the Einayim, comes from the Nekudot of SAG that rose and departed from NHY of AK and became MAN [female waters] in the Nikvey Einayim. Hence the Einayim are the first Hey of HaVaYaH, since the Nekudot of SAG are the first Hey, as above in the words of the ARI. And the last Hey, which rose together with them to the Nikvey Einayim and herself likewise became Einayim — hence the Einayim are the last Hey of HaVaYaH as well. We thus learn that the screen in the Nikvey Einayim is a doubled screen, made of the two Heys together. And it has already been explained that this is the root of the partnership of the quality of mercy with judgment, whose beginning was made (53) in the joining of the two Heys, the first Hey and the bottom Hey, in the Nikvey Einayim.
